audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Faithful, source-grounded draft of 2 Chronicles 26 (KJV verse numbering). Preserves divine name as YHWH, key Hebrew terms (max two per verse), and textual variants noted where present. Numbers and proper names follow the Hebrew witness; Isaiah attribution retained.

verses.restored: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.

familiar.text: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.

verses.restored: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.

familiar.text: He built Eloth, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers.

verses.restored: Sixteen years old was Uzziah when he began to reign; and he reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Sixteen years old was Uzziah when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

verses.restored: And he did that which was right before YHWH, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.

familiar.text: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah did.

notes.title: short
notes.body: ׳Rightness׳ measured by cultic/political continuity with Amaziah.

verses.restored: In the days of Zechariah, who had insight in the visions of God, Uzziah sought God; and as long as he sought YHWH, God made him prosper.

familiar.text: And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Identity of this Zechariah (prophet, court seer, or other) requires witness check.

verses.restored: He went out and made war against the Philistines; he broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod, and he built cities round about Ashdod and among the Philistines.

familiar.text: And he went forth and warred against the Philistines, and brake down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod, and built cities about Ashdod, and among the Philistines.

verses.restored: God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabians who dwell in Gur‑Baal and the Mehunims.

familiar.text: And God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians that dwelt in Gurbaal, and the Mehunims.

verses.restored: The Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah; and his fame reached to the entrance of Egypt, for he became very strong.

familiar.text: And the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah: and his name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt; for he strengthened himself exceedingly.

verses.restored: Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, at the valley gate, and at the turn of the wall, and fortified them.

familiar.text: Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, and at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified them.

verses.restored: He built towers in the desert and dug many wells; for he had much cattle in the lowland and in the plains. He had farmers and vine-dressers in the hills and in Carmel, for he loved the land.

familiar.text: Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry.

verses.restored: Also Uzziah had an army of fighting men that went out in bands, by the number of their muster, by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the ruler, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king's captains.

familiar.text: Moreover Uzziah had an host of fighting men, that went out to war by bands, according to the number of their account by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the ruler, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains.

verses.restored: All the heads of the fathers of the mighty men of valor were two thousand and six hundred.

familiar.text: The whole number of the chief of the fathers of the mighty men of valour were two thousand and six hundred.

verses.restored: Under their hand was an army—three hundred thousand, and seven thousand, and five hundred—mighty in power, to help the king against the enemy.

familiar.text: And under their hand was an army, three hundred thousand and seven thousand and five hundred, that made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.

verses.restored: And Uzziah prepared for them shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slings throughout all the host.

familiar.text: And Uzziah prepared for them throughout all the host shields, and spears, and helmets, and habergeons, and bows, and slings to cast stones.

verses.restored: He made in Jerusalem engines, clever devices, to be on the towers and on the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and large stones; and his fame went out far, for YHWH helped him until he became strong.

familiar.text: And he made in Jerusalem engines, invented by cunning men, to be on the towers and upon the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and great stones withal. And his name spread far abroad; for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong.

verses.restored: But when he was strong his heart was lifted up to his destruction; for he transgressed against YHWH his God, and entered the house of YHWH to burn incense upon the altar of incense.

familiar.text: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense upon the altar of incense.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Transgression framed as hubris leading to cultic overreach.

verses.restored: Then Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of YHWH, valiant men.

familiar.text: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the LORD, that were valiant men:

verses.restored: They stood against King Uzziah and said to him, 'It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to YHWH, but to the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have transgressed; it shall not be for your honor from YHWH God.'

familiar.text: And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the LORD, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from the LORD God.

verses.restored: Then Uzziah was angry; and he had a censer to burn incense in his hand. And while he was angry with the priests, the tzara'at rose up on his forehead before the priests in the house of YHWH, beside the altar of incense.

familiar.text: Then Uzziah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD, from beside the incense altar.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew מצרעת (tzara'at) retained to preserve cultic/disease ambiguity.

verses.restored: And Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked upon him; and behold, he had the disease in his forehead; therefore they thrust him out from there, and he hurried to go out, because YHWH had smitten him.

familiar.text: And Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked upon him, and, behold, he was leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out from thence; yea, himself hasted also to go out, because the LORD had smitten him.

verses.restored: So Uzziah the king was a leper until the day of his death, and he dwelt in a separate house because he was cut off from the house of YHWH; and Jotham his son was over the king's house, judging the people of the land.

familiar.text: And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house, being a leper; for he was cut off from the house of the LORD: and Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.

verses.restored: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, are written by Isaiah the son of Amoz the prophet.

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, did Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, write.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Attribution to Isaiah preserved as in Hebrew; editorial history to be examined.

verses.restored: So Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field of the kings; because they said, 'He is a leper.' And Jotham his son reigned in his stead.

familiar.text: So Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial which belonged to the kings; for they said, He is a leper: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.

translation_notes: Divine name יהוה rendered as YHWH throughout. Hebrew place- and technical-terms transliterated when semantically significant (max two terms per verse). 'Tzara'at' used where Hebrew מצרעת appears to retain cultic/disease ambiguity. Where the Masoretic text offers variants (parenthetical forms in source), variant spellings are noted in source_witness_audit_flags rather than inline.
safety_note: Contains warfare, forced labor/gifts, and disease language (tzara'at). Reader discretion advised.
source_witness_audit_flags: v5 identification and role of ‘Zechariah’ — requires witness check (which Zechariah?).
v7 reading of 'ha'aravim' (הָעַרְבִים) — locate Gur‑Baal and Mehunim in external witnesses.
v10 agricultural terms and 'loved the land' idiom — verify socioeconomic implication in MSS.
v22 claim that Isaiah son of Amoz wrote 'rest of the acts' — later editorial layer possible.
